title: Remove a staple without tearing the papers
instruction: Remove the staple without tearing either sheet.
context: Staple removal is a familiar part of preparing paper records for scanning or reuse. The tool must release the clinched legs without tearing the sheets.
setup: Proposed fixed setup: two white 200 gsm paper sheets, each 210 × 148 × 0.2 mm, on a 210 × 128 × 20 mm document support with a 1.5 × 16 × 8 mm clinch-clearance pocket. In station coordinates, sheet centres are (0.32, 0) and (0.32, 0.012) m, at heights 767.60 and 767.82 mm. A steel staple has a 12.8 mm crown, 6 mm legs and 0.50 × 0.30 mm wire section, clinched through both sheets at x=0.227, y=−0.050 m, through existing 0.8 × 0.6 mm holes. A 108 × 18 × 16 mm steel/ABS forked lever remover rests at x=0.28, y=−0.20 m. The table is 747.5 mm high. All simulation coordinates receive one fixed origin shift before construction, preserving relative geometry. No paper pins or fixed staple. Complete robot extraction and final setup evidence remain unvalidated.
scoring: 0.5 when at least one whole staple leg is clear of both sheets and the preservation checks pass. 1.0 when both legs are clear, the intact staple is at least 10 mm from either sheet, and staple and papers remain released for three seconds. A new tear over 2 mm beyond an original hole, any new cut or puncture elsewhere, a broken staple, altered sheets or invalid evidence gives zero. Creases alone are not tears. The staple may remain in or on a remover that the robot has released onto the work surface.
run_limit: 600 control steps (30 seconds at 20 Hz). The current 584-action extraction-and-release candidate is being tested.
reset_notes: Use fresh matched paper and one fresh staple for every trial. Record both sides before and after. Reuse the remover only while intact.
fidelity: Each sheet has 190 rigid box panels joined by passive bending hinges, approximating flexible 200 gsm paper. A5mg minimum panel mass adds less than5% to sheet mass for numerical stability. The steel staple bends plastically under tool contact. Paper gaps, wire crossings and native fractures are checked; the wire-continuity audit uses actual overlapping steel boxes rather than centreline separation alone. Material values are engineering estimates. Full extraction remains unverified.
